title: Series vs Parallel Explained Simply | PUC Electronics Class 11
description:
One bulb fails on Aarav's old string of festival lights and the whole string goes dark. But when one bulb fails at home, every other light stays on. Why? In this animated lesson we compare the two basic ways to connect parts: in series (one path, like beads on a thread) and in parallel (many paths, like lanes on a road).

On a live breadboard a 12 V supply drives a 4 ohm and a 12 ohm resistor, first in series (the same 0.75 A through both, the voltage shared as 3 V and 9 V; break one and everything stops) and then in parallel (3 A and 1 A adding to 4 A; break one and the other keeps flowing), with the oscilloscope tracking the total current. We derive R = R1 + R2 for series and 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 for parallel step by step, solve a worked example both ways, see why homes are wired in parallel, and finish with the exam trap (always flip 1/R), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a formula card to screenshot.

This is Episode 9 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 2: Principles of Electricity, Network Theorems and AC Principles (Karnataka PUC Electronics).
